title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving and sustainable WASH assistance to vulnerable communities in Beletweyne district, Hiran region

description.narrative: ltpgtWARDI Relief and Development Initiatives (WARDI) proposes a comprehensive, life-saving WASH intervention aimed at addressing the dire humanitarian conditions of drought- and flood-affected populations in Beletweyne district, Hiraan region. The project targets 15,000 drought/conflict-affected people (4,650 women, 3,750 men, 3,600 girls 3,000 boys), including people with disabilities, internally displaced persons (IDPs), women, children, persons with disabilities (PwDs), and marginalized groups who face disproportionate risks due to the breakdown of public services and climate-induced displacement. Based on WARDI’s June 2025 multi-site WASH needs assessment and aligned with the SHF 2025 Standard Allocation strategy, the 12-month intervention aims to reduce morbidity and mortality associated with poor WASH conditions, improve dignity and safety for affected populations, and strengthen local capacity for resilience. The initiative directly contributes to the Somalia 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) and addresses identified gaps in access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services.ltbrgtWARDI will implement a combination of emergency and sustainable WASH solutions, including:ltbrgto Rehabilitation of water infrastructure: One strategic borehole will be rehabilitated with a hybrid solar/diesel system to improve sustainability and cost-efficiency. Ten (3) shallow wells will be rehabilitated. 2 floodproof shallow wells with hand pumps Tuulo Raaxo, Siigaalow) and 1 shallow wells with solar-powered pumps (Deefow west), ensuring safe and accessible water in underserved rural and IDP-populated areas.ltbrgto Sanitation infrastructure: The project will construct 40 gender-sensitive and disability-friendly latrines across schools, health posts, and IDP camps. These latrines will be flood-resistant and include handwashing stations to promote hygiene and reduce disease transmission.ltbrgto Hygiene promotion and supplies: Twenty four community hygiene promoters will be trained to conduct mass campaigns targeting 20,000 people, including house-to-house visits, school outreach, and nutrition/health center education sessions. WARDI will also distribute 500 hygiene kits, including menstrual hygiene items, to high-risk households.ltbrgto Community capacity-building: The project will support and train 9 WASH committees (50% women) to manage water points sustainably, including basic operations and maintenance. Additionally, sanitation sets will be distributed to 10 IDP camps to support environmental health and waste management.ltbrgtThe project takes a protection-integrated approach. Latrine design and placement will prioritize safety, especially for women and girls, with lighting, locks, and strategic locations to prevent gender-based violence. The project will mainstream protection principles by ensuring equitable access, prioritizing feedback mechanisms, and training staff and contractors in Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). WARDI will coordinate closely with the WASH Cluster, OCHA, local authorities, and community-based structures to ensure complementarity, accountability, and sustainability. The project supports localization by recruiting 60% of staff locally, sourcing materials from local markets, and embedding AAP (accountability to the affected populations) mechanisms such as hotlines and community review meetings managed by women-led groups. Ultimately, the project will restore access to safe water and dignified sanitation, mitigate health and protection risks, and strengthen local preparedness and capacity to respond to future shocks. It offers an integrated, community-driven model that is scalable and aligns with both humanitarian imperatives and long-term resilience goals.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
